bc_raptor_wall.blurb: Raptor Wall is a bolted sport face at Begbie Bluffs, a few kilometres down the valley road south of Revelstoke. It is the first wall you meet on the trail up from the parking lot, roughly ten minutes on foot. The 18 routes start with a couple of easy 5.7 and 5.8 lines, build through a solid middle of 5.10s and 5.11s, and top out with a pair of 5.12s. A large roof shelters part of the wall, so it is a handy choice when showers roll through, though it also tends to pull the biggest groups at the bluffs. A good spot for mixed-ability parties.

bc_campground_boulders.blurb: Campground Boulders is a bouldering area beside Comox Lake, a short drive from Cumberland on Vancouver Island. The woods are damp and rainforest-like, so expect moss and carry a brush for the holds. The basalt is mostly firm. All 18 problems are boulders, running from V0 to a single V4, with the bulk between V1 and V3, which makes it friendly for newer boulderers while still offering a few harder lines. A smaller cluster, the Sherman Boulders, sits nearby just before the lake. Plenty of boulders are still undeveloped.

bc_west_side_boulders.blurb: West Side Boulders is the western cluster of the bouldering at Cypress Falls in West Vancouver, tucked into a creek-canyon trail system that sees plenty of walkers. Problems begin at a conspicuous slab boulder only a few minutes from the trailhead. The 18 problems skew easy, with many at V0 to V2 and a handful stepping up toward V4 and V5, so it works well as a short session or a warm-up. The canyon stays cool through summer, but the boulders take a week or more to dry after heavy rain and can be mossy.

bc_pale_face.blurb: Pale Face is a compact boulder cluster in the Hunter Creek area of the Fraser Valley, near Hope and Chilliwack, found by following a forest trail east of the Goldfinger boulder. It has a highball flavour, with flat landings and mellow topouts that make it a friendly introduction to taller problems. The 18 problems run from a VB through the mid grades and on to a few very hard lines, with the largest share between V1 and V5. Bring several pads, and watch for nettles and other irritating plants along the approach in warm months.

bc_boulder_zone_1_bz1.blurb: Boulder Zone 1 is the largest of the zones in the Buntzen Lake boulders, in the hills east of Vancouver. Large blocks that broke away from the bluffs above lie scattered in the forest, and this zone holds the biggest of them, with some handsome lines. The 18 problems are all bouldering, running from V0 up to a V10, with about half sitting at V0 to V3 and a handful of hard problems in the V5 to V10 range. A good mix for a group with a wide spread of ability.

bc_hall_siding.blurb: Hall Siding is a roadside sport crag in the West Kootenay, about 17 km south of Nelson along Highway 6, and the face can be seen from the pavement. The wall is steep and sharp, and it cools off in the late part of the day, which suits warm afternoons. It also tends to stay dry in light rain. Of the 18 routes, almost all are bolted and two are trad. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, but the weight sits in the 5.10s and 5.11s, so it suits climbers who already lead comfortably in that range.
